Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: one opaque, continuous graphite-metal ridge material for a high-resolution pure 2D game in a restrained futuristic Earth-base style, consistent with the accepted metal in reference 2.

Image 1 is a flat UV layout guide, not artwork: U runs horizontally, N runs downward. Image 2 supplies only the graphite metal identity, subtle fine grain and daylight tone. Do not copy its vertical panel grooves or its geometry.

Create a 1024 x 1536 opaque texture sheet filling the entire canvas. The single useful ridge core is x111.170..912.830, y201.442..1334.558. This is ONE uninterrupted surface, not several stacked strips. Continue the same material through all surrounding overscan. Remove all reference text, colored lines and borders.

The visible volume must come only from baked 2D material lighting across N: a moderately dark upper shoulder; a broad, soft rounded highlight centered within y424..591; then a long smooth falloff toward the lower edge. The highlight should read as a curved metal ridge at native game scale, not as a narrow white line or a flat linear light-to-dark ramp. Within the final approximately 14 raw pixels of the core, y1321..1335, add a quiet dark inner contact shade that continues into the lower overscan. Do not draw an exterior silhouette, projecting lip, object edge or cast shadow outside this material sheet.

Keep this entire light profile constant horizontally: the two vertical core cuts must join as a continuous ridge without a seam, left-to-right lighting drift, panel division or bright join. Fine metal grain may vary softly, but no isolated scratches, repeating marks, bolts or raised details. Calm graphite gray, satin metal, subdued highlights, clean modern construction; no white chrome, soil-yellow stone, roof tiles, orange rust, lettering or objects. No perspective camera, wall, building, corner, transparent background, vertical seams or end caps.

Keep the flat guide proportions and the single continuous surface. Do not fit a pictured ridge object into the rectangle. This is already-lit 2D art, not a uniform albedo or a recovered 3D surface.
